findings.title: Local cache set before DB write allows bypassing device limit
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, the local cache entry is set (line 87: `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})`) before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called. If `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (because the device is new and the limit is hit), the error propagates and authentication fails. However, the cache entry persists for 29 minutes. On the very next request from the same device, `tagDeviceUI` will find the cache hit at line 83 and return nil immediately, never reaching the database. This means the device limit is effectively bypassed after the first rejected attempt — the second request within the cache TTL will authenticate successfully despite the device not existing in the database.

findings.title: TOCTOU race between CountDevices and INSERT allows exceeding device limit
findings.body: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the check `count >= s.deviceLimit` (line 115) and the subsequent INSERT (lines 122-153) are not atomic. Under concurrent load, multiple goroutines can each observe `count < deviceLimit`, then all proceed to INSERT, causing the actual number of devices to exceed the configured limit. A transactional approach or database-level constraint would be needed to enforce the limit reliably.

findings.title: TagDevice moved from async goroutine to synchronous authentication path
findings.body: Previously `TagDevice` was called in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout, making it fire-and-forget so database latency did not block authentication. Now it runs synchronously in the `Authenticate` method. Every anonymous request will wait for the database round-trip (including the `CountDevices` query when a limit is set) before authentication completes. Under high anonymous traffic or database latency spikes, this directly increases request latency for all anonymous users.

findings.title: ErrDeviceLimitReached returned for non-limit scenarios in updateDevice
findings.body: In `updateDevice`, `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned whenever `rowsAffected == 0`. This can also occur when the device exists in the database but its `updated_at` falls outside the BETWEEN window (e.g., the device was last seen more than 30 days ago). In that case the error is semantically wrong — the device is known but stale, not blocked by a limit. This could cause confusing error handling upstream and might incorrectly block a returning device whose record simply aged out of the window.

findings.title: Duplicated anonymousDeviceExpiration constant risks drift
findings.body: The constant `anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour` is now defined independently in both `anonstore/database.go` (line 16) and `api/api.go` (line 18). If one is updated without the other, the API listing window and the store's expiration logic will diverge silently. This should be a single shared constant.
